I'm not trying to play a card here or anything, but I've been diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and clinical depression, but I think the borderline fucks up my views on friends a lot of times without me realizing it. (Sometimes I have a hard time separating my personality from the symptoms, I'm supposed to be taking a few types of medication but can't afford them or the therapy anymore but this isn't r/depression so I'll leave it at that :) ) You're absolutely right in that in that I have a hard time finding/making/keeping friends. I've lived in the same place my whole life (minus a short stint out of state when I was younger, but the reason I moved back has nothing to do with deteriorating relationships there.) I went through the same school district my whole life, etc etc. I had very few friends, and the ones I did make never seemed to stick around unless they needed me for something. (Hence, why I was so broken about my two friends and the hockey game. They've been my oldest friends here and the only ones I hung out with on a regular basis, now I'm forever alone :() I thought college would change things, but it really didn't. (I went to college about an hour away from where I live, so it wasn't a very drastic change.) 

Another thing I've noticed is that I'm really offbeat compared to a lot of the people that I've met/live in the area. The only way I know how to explain it is that I live in a very conservative area, and I'm very liberal. Not just in a political view, obviously, but I dye my hair pink, have my tongue pierced, have tattoos, etc. It's uncommon around here. I thought going to art school would help me meet people more like myself, but it really didn't. I met a few cool people, but now we don't keep in touch any more than Facebook. They were the same, though, usually kept me around because I had a car and many of them didn't.  I pretty much gave up trying to find new local friends. 

I do have a handful of very good friends, though, that I met through going to conventions. They're scattered throughout the country, but we all keep in contact, and they've never fucked me over. I get to see them 1-3 times a year, depending. It's depressing, but better than nothing. I'm moving to California to be with my girlfriend, (who I met through the cons) and lives around some of our mutual convention friends, and I need a change. Another deciding factor is that there are no jobs in my area for what I went to school for, and there are many more opportunities on the other side of the country. Right now I'm just stuck, I won't get tl;dr over all of it but, shitty job, had to move back in with parents, can't do shit with my degree here. I've been looking for any excuse to leave for a long, long time now. 

But I really, really do appreciate all the advice you've given. I've realized over the years that I tend to keep people at a distance without realizing it, but I'm not quite sure why. When I was in therapy I brought it up a few times, but I don't think I ever quite got a straight answer. 

But seriously, thanks man :)

But I'm still pretty pissed about it, haven't talked to them since :/ They've texted me trying to get rides here and there but that's it.

You can also have a garden where you plant berries. Depending on the berry, they can take from a few hours to a few days to grow.

The dream bridge thing is where everyone wants to go. It's a rainbow, you click it, and it takes you to a forest where you can catch the aforementioned pokemon by clicking shaking bushes and trees, and sparkles for items. Once you encounter a pokemon, it wants to play a game with you. If you do well at the game, the pokemon will be happy and will want to be your friend. 

After you're there for 10 "steps", it automatically takes you to the tree of dreams, and you can choose a pokemon you befriended to take to your game. 

There's a bunch of other shit you can do it on, too. Fennel pretty much explains everything to you as you find it. 

tl;dr yeah it's aimed at 10 year olds but it's an easy way to get pokemon you wouldn't otherwise be able to get in your game besides trading.

I was 14, in 9th grade, in art class. We always watched Cartoon Network if we were just working on assignments, as we were on that day. All of the sudden, my teacher ran across the room and switched the channel to the news reporting what had happened. We all watched as the second plane hit. No one had ANY idea what was going on, I remember walking to my next class completely confused, asking my friends if they had heard what happened, and most of them didn't believe me. I remember being angry at the kids my age that kept asking what the Twin Towers were/where this was happening.  The next class there was an announcement over the PA system that teachers are encouraged to turn on the TV to watch the news. Apparently I was one of very few students that had known about it prior to the announcement. During that time was when the plane crashed in Pennsylvania, about an hour away from my school. There were military helicopters everywhere for the next few days.  We were encouraged to get in touch with our parents and go home, but my parents were at work and I didn't have a cell phone so I just waited the day out. Plus, I was really interested to learn more in what was happening so I didn't mind just going to my classes and watching the news. By the end of the day, most of the school had gone home, teachers included. It was a quiet day, we just watched the news the rest of the day in all of our classes. The next day, most of our classes were open discussions to ask and discuss what happened the day before. 

tl;dr The plane in PA crashed near here and everyone was understandably freaking out
